description:
List bulk AP migrations

Detected bulk migrations between Access Points, largest first. A cohort is a gap-≤3-day island of (from_provider, to_provider) mover days that clears three thresholds: at least 25 participants, at least 40 % of them on the busiest day (which rejects a steady drip), and at most 20 active days for the pair over the trailing 40 days (which rejects a recurring partnership).

Every day is the PROBE-OBSERVATION day — the day the change scan saw the SMP record change, not the day the migration was executed — so a cohort is always a `[first_day, last_day]` range and `peak_day` is the busiest observation day. Render the range, never a single date.

`top_country` is derived from the ICD prefix of the participant identifiers, not from business-card country fields. `merge_suspect` marks a cohort large enough (or whose source provider no longer resolves in the directory) to be a provider merge or a renamed provider rather than that many independent customer decisions — the canonical case is Sovos → Sage, 10,574 participants. Such rows are data events, not customer decisions; verify one before quoting it. The flag is a CURRENT judgment, re-evaluated on every recompute, not frozen at detection.

PLATFORM MOVES. A mover is a platform move when the platform that serves the participant stayed and only the certificate Seat changed: it is not a customer decision. The verdict is per DIRECTED provider pair (from → to), over all its movers since 2026-08-02, with one of two reasons (`same_host`, `sub_provider`): at least 90% of the movers whose endpoint host can be compared (5 or more, and at least 50% of all movers of the pair) kept their endpoint host, or at least 90% of 25 or more movers still carry, at the new provider, the sub-provider brand of the provider they left. It is a CURRENT judgment, computed again on every rollup cycle. A cohort of such a pair has `platform_move: true`. It stays in the list. A Vendor's cohorts (`provider=v-<slug>`) are not changed and have no `platform_move`.

`from`/`to` are OVERLAP bounds (a cohort counts when its range intersects the window), defaulting to the trailing 90 days the detector re-clusters. Mover history begins 2026-07-24, so no cohort predates it. `id` is a request-lifetime handle for the participant drill-down — never persist one.

cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor returned as `next_cursor` by the previous page.

direction.description: Which side of the `provider` filter to take: `in` = cohorts the provider received, `out` = cohorts it lost, `both` = either. Only meaningful together with `provider`.

from.description: Inclusive lower bound of the observation window (`YYYY-MM-DD` UTC); a cohort matches when its `last_day` is at or after it. Defaults to 90 days ago.

limit.description: Page size, clamped to [1, 200]. Defaults to 50.

merge_suspect.description: How to treat probable provider merges / slug changes: `include` (default), `exclude` for real customer migrations only, or `only` to review the flagged rows.

min_participants.description: Only cohorts with at least this many participants. The detector's own floor is 25, so a lower value cannot surface smaller groups. With a Vendor key as `provider` the floor and the default are 5.

provider.description: Only cohorts involving this Provider key (`/v1/aps/{key}`). Matches EITHER side unless `direction` narrows it. A Vendor key (`v-<slug>`) returns the cohorts of that Vendor's movers instead: each item has `kind: "vendor"`, one side of the pair is the Vendor, and the floor is 5 participants. Vendor cohorts are in no other response of this endpoint.

to.description: Inclusive upper bound of the observation window (`YYYY-MM-DD` UTC); a cohort matches when its `first_day` is at or before it. Defaults to today.

name: list_cohort_moves
